newsitem.title: USA: Stocks extend powerful rally into second day.
newsitem.headline: Stocks extend powerful rally into second day.

text.p: The stock market soared again on Wednesday, extending the previous session's run into the record books on Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comment that the central bank would not raise interest rates soon.
The Dow Jones industrial average, which powered ahead 2 percent Tuesday, shot up 69.91 points to 8,131.56 in early morning trading.
Tuesday's surge lifted the Dow 155 points to a new high of 8,061.65, beating last Wednesday's record finish of 8,038.88 and setting its 33rd milestone so far this year.
In the bond market, the Treasury's key 30-year bond was little changed after soaring 1-22/32 on Tuesday, which cut its yield to 6.41 percent -- the lowest since Dec. 5 of last year.
In his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on the economy to Congress, Greenspan said the Fed would raise interest rates if needed to head off inflation, but suggested that might not happen anytime soon.
Greenspan spent much of his testimony discussing the reasons behind the recent stellar performance of the U.S. economy and whether that can be maintained.

Unlike in his last Humphrey Hawkins testimony in February and in a speech in December, Greenspan did not caution financial markets that they might be "irrationally exuberant" on the outlook for the economy and corporate profits.
But he did make clear the Fed was watching the economy closely for any signs that the recent good news on inflation was coming to an end.

The Fed chief returns to Congress on Wednesday to address the Senate Banking Committee in the second leg of his mandatory, semiannual testimony. He will repeat his formal remarks and then answer questions from senators.
"This should be a restatement, a replay of yesterday," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "It will probably be a non-event."
More solid quarterly earnings results would also boost stock prices.
Several technology companies reported above-forecast results late Tuesday, boosting the Nasdaq composite index 13.37 points to 1,577.23.
Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Co. reported earnings of $1.01 per share vs. 91 cents a share a year ago. But its stock lost 1-1/4 to 99-1/16 in early NYSE trading.
